chunks: And from him, from Ibn Fazzal, who said:

Ali ibn Asbaat said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) while we were listening: 'We had not rested (in the Muarras), so Ibn Al-Qasim ibn Al-Fudayl informed us that he had not rested, and that he asked you, so you ordered him to return to the Muarras so that he might rest therein.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.'

He said to him: 'If we leave and rest therein, what should we do?' He said: 'You should pray therein and lie down.' And Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) used to pray therein after the night prayer (Al-Atamah).

Muhammad said to him: 'If one passes by it at a time other than that of a prescribed prayer?' He said: 'After Al-Asr.' It was said: 'Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was asked about this, so he said: 'Permission for this is granted only in the two cycles of the Tawaf (circumambulation), for Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) did so.' And he said: 'One should stay until the time for the prayer enters.'

He said: 'I said to him: 'May I be sacrificed for you! So the one who passes by it at night or by day, does he rest therein, or is the resting only at night?' He said: 'If one passes by it at night or by day, let him rest therein.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for praying and resting at the Prophet's Muarras?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of resting (I'tirās) at the Prophet’s resting place, affirming that it is valid day or night, though Imam al-Rida (AS) specifically practiced praying there after the night prayer (Al-Atamah). It distinguishes this general resting from the specific concession for the two rak'ahs of Tawaf, which are restricted to their prescribed times, highlighting the flexibility of devotional practices at sacred sites in Shia jurisprudence.
